'''Enecogen power station''' is an operating power station of at least 870-megawatts (MW) in Rotterdam, Zuid-Holland, Netherlands.

{{#widget:ObservableOwnershipTree|}}

==Background==

The power station is owned by Enecogen, a partnership between utilities Eneco Energie and Dong Energy, each with a 50% stake. Construction of the plant started in May 2009 and began commercial operation in late 2011.<ref>[http://www.power-technology.com/projects/enecogen-ccgt/ "Enecogen CCGT Power Station, Netherlands,"] Power-technology.com, accessed Feb 2013.</ref>

C.Gen originally planned for the power station to be fueled by coal.{{fact}}

In 2017 DONG Energy changed its name to Ørsted and began divesting its fossil fuel assets.<ref>[https://orsted.com/en/about-us/about-orsted/about-our-name About Our Name], Ørsted, accessed Apr 8, 2021</ref> In 2018 Castleton Commodities International (CCI) bought Orsted's 50% stake in the project.<ref>[https://www.cci.com/assets/power Power Assets], CCI, accessed Apr 8, 2021</ref>

As part of its "ambition [...] to become climate neutral [...] in 2035" Eneco has proposed running Enecogen on "Green Gas", implementing CCUS, running the plants on Hydrogen, or a combination thereof.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eneco.com/wat-we-doen/duurzame-bronnen/enecogen/|title=Enecogen|website=www.eneco.com|language=en|access-date=2021-11-27}}</ref>
